question: do prediction-error peaks mark real event boundaries?
ground_truth: CARLA pose-derived motion-regime changes (start/stop/turn); never from the image

raw_residual.verdict: measures how fast things are moving, not when the pattern changes

divisively_normalised.verdict: confound removed; boundary recall 2.7x chance but only half of episodes beat chance, and the negative accel correlation shows the division over-corrects

testbed_limit: CARLA episodes are 40 frames (~2s), barely one event. City Sample has 2,900-frame runs but no pose, so no ground truth for when an event began.
not_claimed: that this segments video into events well enough to abstract over

explainer_testbed.what: generated informational video with the answer key built in; owner clarified the videos they meant are conceptual/knowledge channels, not live-action footage

prediction_error: 38.5 found / 13 true - fires on every sub-step

replacement_self_motion_removed: 26.8/13 - slight gain only, and the same compensation DAMAGED build 1.000 -> 0.692

explainer_testbed.divisive_normalisation: helped a lot on CARLA, HURT on explainer pans (0.808 -> 0.692); data-dependent, not a universal fix

long_real_testbed.what: 21,032 frames / 240s of City Sample; boundaries RECORDED at the moment ATANOR's own motor command changed - no threshold, no percentile, nothing inferred
long_real_testbed.verdict: all three ~1.4x chance, all firing 3x too often; the 5.4x on generated explainer video does NOT transfer to real 3D footage

standing_verdict: replacement-vs-addition is a real measured advance on explainer-style video (1.7x -> 5.4x on build, exact boundary count). On real footage of a moving body it is 1.5x chance and unsolved.
